Extortion In The Villages

By: Sipha Kema | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Local business owners in the Eastern Cape rural towns living in fear for the past two years

Unique Selling Point:
Tsomo, Cofimvaba, Nqamkwe and eNgcobo these are four small rural towns situated about 29km from each other in the Former Transkei. These small towns have a lot in common like hardware stores being a popular and driving force for the towns’ economy and struggling job creation.

However, two years ago these rural towns got a lot more in common when a new type of crime syndicate moved into these little towns. Letters were sent to all hardware stores telling them that they are not allowed to deliver any stock and supplies to customers. A company known as Masimanyane (the alleged extorters) would from now on service all customer deliveries in and around these small towns. This new and unheard of company also demanded all hardware stores owners get rid of all the delivery staff (drivers etc) to prove they would use Masimanyane’s services, this meaning getting rid of staff members who are breadwinners and have been part of these stores for years. However the delivery system proved to be an impossible task for them after customers complained about the pricing and delayed deliveries.

Following failed meeting after meeting, Masimanyane delivery service then decided, starting in Engcobo to set fire to any business trucks doing their own deliveries. From Engcobo they moved to Cofimvaba doing the same thing burning every truck doing deliveries. This group also started terrorizing the drivers who were out on deliveries by not allowing them in various locations. Stoning the trucks and threatening their lives.

After COVID19 regulations eased, the extorters continued with their reign of terror and moved into Tsomo and burned delivery trucks there too. Two weeks ago, they cut the security fence to the case study’s yard and set three of their trucks on fire at 12.39am on Sunday Morning 24/07/2022 (two men are seen on the CCTV entering the premises, one holding a cannister).

Some of the businesses are still paying for their burnt trucks but have had to purchase new trucks to deliver stock customers, delivery service is the main service for these businesses.

Should these local businesses fail, many will lose their livelihoods and are the main breadwinners. The Hardware stores across these rural towns are the main employment industry.

Script:


{wait three\four seconds then first VO}

VO: It’s a Thursday evening in a small town in the Eastern Cape…
VO: A man emerges from the darkness and breaks into a hardware compound….
VO:Seconds later… a vehicle is in flames…[pause] but this isn’t an isolated incident… hardware stores in small Eastern Cape towns like Tsomo, Cofimvaba, Ngcobo, are under attack… and delivery trucks are the target…

UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME); BUSINESS OWNER
03:11 – 03:15
It started at about 2018/2019…

UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME); BUSINESS OWNER
03:32 – 03:49
One day I got to work, I was handed a piece of paper by a lady and on the paper was a telephone number, and the lady said to me “You phone that telephone number for your deliveries. You are no longer going to do deliveries.”

VO: Jack, not his real name, is a well known businessman in these parts. He’s asked that we protect his identity.

UPSOUND: MASA
08:34 - 08:40
Why did you even call that number because it looks like she came in to intimidate you, this wasn't a business proposition.

UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME); BUSINESS OWNER
08: 42 - 09:10
No, it definitely wasn't a business proposition but I had heard one or two stories from other towns where the same thing had happened, trucks had been burnt. And people were also prevented from doing deliveries.

VO: But Jack didn’t heed the warning…

UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME); BUSINESS OWNER
12:26 - 12:42
I continued delivering. And my drivers I explained to them that please, if they come across anything, the first thing they need to do is get out of the truck and run.

UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME);
BUSINESS OWNER
14:39 - 14:44
It wasn't a week later when my trucks were burnt.

UPSOUND: “NOZI” (NOT REAL NAME); EMPLOYEE
02:17 – 02:41
SUBTITLES
They were forceful. They came in large numbers and were confrontational. The I say they were forceful; they could have politely requested an appointment with my employer my of barging in.

VO: Nozi works in one of the hardware stores.
When her boss also ignored instructions, there were consequences…

UPSOUND: “NOZI” (NOT REAL NAME); EMPLOYEE
SUBTITLES
08:12 - 08:38
I received a call around midnight saying the store was on fire. I called a colleague who lives closer to the store, I thought the actual store was burning down. The person called me back saying the trucks were on fire, not the store.

UPSOUND: “NOZI” (NOT REAL NAME); EMPLOYEE
14:25 - 14:40
We are afraid, we really are afraid because we don't know what else could happen now or what to expect.

VO: As these rural communities continue to grow… so too is the construction industry… and hardware stores have never been busier…
VO: …. on average, a truck loads material worth R40 000 per delivery. And, because villages are so far apart, a single delivery can cost up to R3000.

UPSOUND: MASA 01:03 – 01:08
Has the hardware industry grown in the community, has it seen more businesses popping up?
UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME); BUSINESS OWNER
02:13 – 02:15
People have found that it’s a lucrative business…
UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME)
BUSINESS OWNER 02:34 – 02:42
The community are building all the time, so there is definitely, I would say that they do a lot of DIY.

VO:... Corrugated iron sheets, bricks, cement: building materials destined for far flung villages. Add the delivery charge, and it becomes a highly profitable enterprise
… and lucrative businesses often attract unwanted attention; sinister networks looking for their slice of the action. Enter Masiphathisane, an organised group of violent community members.
Meaning “ let’s take care of each other” Masiphathisane is running a mafia-style extortion racket in the Province.

UPSOUND: “INGA” (NOT REAL NAME); DELIVERY DRIVER
01:01 – 01:12
SUBTITLES
In 2019, I was chased by the people who work for Masiphathisane while I was out for delivery. They stopped me and asked where I was going…they told me to turn back to the store.

VO: This driver, we’re calling Inga, says the job is a risk to life.

UPSOUND: “INGA” (NOT REAL NAME); DELIVERY DRIVER
01:45 – 01:53
SUBTITLES
They’ve made our jobs unbearable; they chase us on the roads and now we’re scared to make deliveries.

LINK MASA: It seems these truck drivers are caught between a rock and a hard place, it’s either they continue working to feed their families and face threats of intimidation and fear. Or, they quit their jobs.(END)

VO: So who’s pulling the strings? Who’s responsible for this upheaval? The answer might surprise you. PAUSE This is Nontando Plaaitjie: active church elder, a pillar of her local community…
VO: … and alleged Masiphathisane mastermind, instigator of the campaign of intimidation and violence unleashed on some local businesses.

UPSOUND: “NOZI” (NOT REAL NAME); EMPLOYEE
04:38 - 04:49
SUBTITLES
She doesn't come off as dangerous because we thought she's a religious woman, a churchgoer

VO: Looks, it seems, can be deceiving: beneath the respectable exterior is a woman of steel, apparently unafraid of getting her own hands dirty.
VO: It’s a simple enough extortion racket…Plaaitjies and her band of merry men, deliver letters of demand to the hardware store owners… “hand over your truck delivery services… or else… “

UPSOUND: “NOZI” (NOT REAL NAME); EMPLOYEE
04:18 - 04:26
She was quite vocal, at the forefront leading the group in delivering letters, she’s actually running this whole thing.

VO: For weeks, our team worked to track her down… but Plaaitjie proved surprisingly slippery…
That is until we spotted her at a church event eNgcobo… apparently rattled, she agreed to speak to our producer in her car…

PLAAITJIE 05:33 - 05:36
I was NEVER there when they delivered those letters. The letters were delivered by Masiphathisane's truck drivers…

UPSOUND: PRODUCER
05:37 - 05:40
But the store owners say you were there and they showed us the CCTV Footage…

UPSOUND: NONTANDO PLAAITJIE;
(SHE cuts in)05:41 - 05:47
I only went to Build-It, that's it…maybe King Hardware.

VO: In a corner, Plaaitjies spilled the beans.

UPSOUND: NONTANDO PLAAITJIE;
0:26 - 0:30
The hardware stores around here are owned by foreign nationals and white people.

UPSOUND: NONTANDO PLAAITJIE;
01:35 - 01:50
Our municipality suggested that since it's our black people who work at these hardware stores we split the delivery services 50/50. We said we don't mind as long as we also get to make money but we'll monitor the deliveries ourselves.

VO: She calls it monitoring … but business owners call it extortion…
Plaaitjie insists that she runs a legitimate business… contracted by a number of hardware stores to make deliveries…
Not so, says Jack. He maintains Plaaitjie even demanded that he fire some of his employees…

UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME);
BUSINESS OWNER 03:51 – 04:18
I said to her, you know, my biggest problem is the people that work for me. I have drivers, I have conductors; they’re the gentlemen that go with the driver, they offload. I said then what do I do with my staff? And she said to me that I must give them a package and I must send them home.

UPSOUND: MASA
Wait? A person you've never met before, just comes and demands you dismiss your staff?

UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME);
BUSINESS OWNER
That's exactly what she did.

VO: Despite the fear and intimidation, business owners in the area have attempted to negotiate with Plaaitjies and her infamous group…

UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME)
BUSINESS OWNER 11:04 - 11:15
In one of the meetings I went to I was asked to keep quiet and sit down…. [gives this a beat or two before the next VO]

UPSOUND: PRODUCER
07:13 - 07:17 (Plaaitjie cuts in)
Why are you doing this? Why this bus…(SHE cuts in)

UPSOUND: NONTANDO PLAAITJIE
07:17 - 07:34
Because of the economy - it's bad. We are struggling. We can't just sit back and watch our trucks remain stationary. This is our government, we can't allow people from outside to benefit more than us. We aren't asking for much…
VO: That’s worth another listen…

UPSOUND: NONTANDO PLAAITJIE
07:17 - 07:34
This is our government, we can't allow people from outside to benefit more than us.

VO: And there it was…. about as close to an admission as we were ever going to get…
The intimidation and coercion have left hardware store owners feeling helpless… while police in this area seemingly look the other way… or worse.

UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME);
BUSINESS OWNER
11:24 - 11:35
The police got involved, I had a meeting with the station Commander. I did speak with the station commander. At one of the meetings the station commander was present.

LINK MASA: This is the Tsomo Police Station, it’s surrounded by many hardware stores within stones throw, yet all of this is happening uninterrupted, right in front of them.

UPSOUND: “NOZI” (NOT REAL NAME);
EMPLOYEE
09:08 - 09:11
SUBTITLES
When we went to the police station to report the incident, both gates were locked with a padlock.
MASA
09:11 - 09:11
At the police station?
NOZI
09:11 - 09:35
SUBTITLES
(SHE OVERLAPS MASA DURING THE INTERVIEW)
At the police station…We rattle the padlock until two police officers appear from the top gate. We informed them about the trucks that were on fire, the police officer's response was "We aren't firefighters" so there's nothing they could do.
LINK MASA: The people we’ve spoken to say the police in this area are basically non-existent. We’ve been trying to get answers from them but we’ve been given the run around and gotten a basically, blase attitude about something that’s very serious and dangerous.
Ultimately, they opted for a written response, avoiding an on-camera interview.

VO: The police say no new cases have been reported against Plaaitjies and that there was no evidence linking her to a crime in a previous report.
They added that one case of arson involving a truck was investigated, but that there was insufficient evidence…

VO: While the police continue to drag their feet, these hardware store owners continue to live in fear…

UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME);
BUSINESS OWNER
26:14 - 26:32
I've decided to speak out because I want it to be exposed, I want people to see what is happening and maybe it being exposed there might be something done about it.

THE END
STRAPS
“JACK” (NOT REAL NAME)
“NOZI” (NOT REAL NAME)
“INGA” (NOT REAL NAME)
BRIGADIER THEMBINKOSI KINANA;
SAPS EC SPOKESPERSON
VOICE OF NONTANDO PLAAITJIE MASIPHATHISANE CHAIR
FIN!!!!

UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME); BUSINESS OWNER 08: 42 - 09:10 No, it definitely wasn't a business proposition but I had heard one or two stories from other towns where the same thing had happened, trucks had been burnt. VO: Nozi works in one of the hardware stores. UPSOUND: “NOZI” (NOT REAL NAME); EMPLOYEE 14:25 - 14:40 We are afraid, we really are afraid because we don't know what else could happen now or what to expect. UPSOUND: “INGA” (NOT REAL NAME); DELIVERY DRIVER 01:45 – 01:53 SUBTITLES They’ve made our jobs unbearable; they chase us on the roads and now we’re scared to make deliveries. PAUSE This is Nontando Plaaitjie: active church elder, a pillar of her local community… VO: … and alleged Masiphathisane mastermind, instigator of the campaign of intimidation and violence unleashed on some local businesses. UPSOUND: “NOZI” (NOT REAL NAME); EMPLOYEE 04:38 - 04:49 SUBTITLES She doesn't come off as dangerous because we thought she's a religious woman, a churchgoer VO: Looks, it seems, can be deceiving: beneath the respectable exterior is a woman of steel, apparently unafraid of getting her own hands dirty. UPSOUND: NONTANDO PLAAITJIE; 01:35 - 01:50 Our municipality suggested that since it's our black people who work at these hardware stores we split the delivery services 50/50. VO: She calls it monitoring … but business owners call it extortion… Plaaitjie insists that she runs a legitimate business… contracted by a number of hardware stores to make deliveries… Not so, says Jack. He maintains Plaaitjie even demanded that he fire some of his employees… UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME); BUSINESS OWNER 03:51 – 04:18 I said to her, you know, my biggest problem is the people that work for me. I have drivers, I have conductors; they’re the gentlemen that go with the driver, they offload. I said then what do I do with my staff? And she said to me that I must give them a package and I must send them home. UPSOUND: MASA Wait? A person you've never met before, just comes and demands you dismiss your staff? UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME); BUSINESS OWNER That's exactly what she did. VO: Despite the fear and intimidation, business owners in the area have attempted to negotiate with Plaaitjies and her infamous group… UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME) BUSINESS OWNER 11:04 - 11:15 In one of the meetings I went to I was asked to keep quiet and sit down…. [gives this a beat or two before the next VO] UPSOUND: PRODUCER 07:13 - 07:17 (Plaaitjie cuts in) Why are you doing this? Why this bus…(SHE cuts in) UPSOUND: NONTANDO PLAAITJIE 07:17 - 07:34 Because of the economy - it's bad. We are struggling. We can't just sit back and watch our trucks remain stationary. This is our government, we can't allow people from outside to benefit more than us. We aren't asking for much… VO: That’s worth another listen… UPSOUND: NONTANDO PLAAITJIE 07:17 - 07:34 This is our government, we can't allow people from outside to benefit more than us. VO: And there it was…. about as close to an admission as we were ever going to get… The intimidation and coercion have left hardware store owners feeling helpless… while police in this area seemingly look the other way… or worse. UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME); BUSINESS OWNER 11:24 - 11:35 The police got involved, I had a meeting with the station Commander. I did speak with the station commander. At one of the meetings the station commander was present. LINK MASA: This is the Tsomo Police Station, it’s surrounded by many hardware stores within stones throw, yet all of this is happening uninterrupted, right in front of them. UPSOUND: “NOZI” (NOT REAL NAME); EMPLOYEE 09:08 - 09:11 SUBTITLES When we went to the police station to report the incident, both gates were locked with a padlock. MASA 09:11 - 09:11 At the police station? NOZI 09:11 - 09:35 SUBTITLES (SHE OVERLAPS MASA DURING THE INTERVIEW) At the police station…We rattle the padlock until two police officers appear from the top gate. We informed them about the trucks that were on fire, the police officer's response was "We aren't firefighters" so there's nothing they could do. LINK MASA: The people we’ve spoken to say the police in this area are basically non-existent. We’ve been trying to get answers from them but we’ve been given the run around and gotten a basically, blase attitude about something that’s very serious and dangerous. Ultimately, they opted for a written response, avoiding an on-camera interview. VO: The police say no new cases have been reported against Plaaitjies and that there was no evidence linking her to a crime in a previous report. They added that one case of arson involving a truck was investigated, but that there was insufficient evidence… VO: While the police continue to drag their feet, these hardware store owners continue to live in fear… UPSOUND: “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME); BUSINESS OWNER 26:14 - 26:32 I've decided to speak out because I want it to be exposed, I want people to see what is happening and maybe it being exposed there might be something done about it. THE END STRAPS “JACK” (NOT REAL NAME) “NOZI” (NOT REAL NAME) “INGA” (NOT REAL NAME) BRIGADIER THEMBINKOSI KINANA; SAPS EC SPOKESPERSON VOICE OF NONTANDO PLAAITJIE MASIPHATHISANE CHAIR FIN!!!!

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Local business owners in the Eastern Cape rural towns living in fear for the past two years
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Tsomo, Cofimvaba, Nqamkwe and eNgcobo these are four small rural towns situated about 29km from each other in the Former Transkei. These small towns have a lot in common like hardware stores being a popular and driving force for the towns’ economy and struggling job creation. However, two years ago these rural towns got a lot more in common when a new type of crime syndicate moved into these little towns. Letters were sent to all hardware stores telling them that they are not allowed to deliver any stock and supplies to customers. A company known as Masimanyane (the alleged extorters) would from now on service all customer deliveries in and around these small towns. This new and unheard of company also demanded all hardware stores owners get rid of all the delivery staff (drivers etc) to prove they would use Masimanyane’s services, this meaning getting rid of staff members who are breadwinners and have been part of these stores for years. However the delivery system proved to be an impossible task for them after customers complained about the pricing and delayed deliveries. Following failed meeting after meeting, Masimanyane delivery service then decided, starting in Engcobo to set fire to any business trucks doing their own deliveries. From Engcobo they moved to Cofimvaba doing the same thing burning every truck doing deliveries. This group also started terrorizing the drivers who were out on deliveries by not allowing them in various locations. Stoning the trucks and threatening their lives. After COVID19 regulations eased, the extorters continued with their reign of terror and moved into Tsomo and burned delivery trucks there too. Two weeks ago, they cut the security fence to the case study’s yard and set three of their trucks on fire at 12.39am on Sunday Morning 24/07/2022 (two men are seen on the CCTV entering the premises, one holding a cannister). Some of the businesses are still paying for their burnt trucks but have had to purchase new trucks to deliver stock customers, delivery service is the main service for these businesses. Should these local businesses fail, many will lose their livelihoods and are the main breadwinners. The Hardware stores across these rural towns are the main employment industry.
